personas.name: Tomasz

personas.hidden_agenda: Wants to bring his partner to the conference city

personas.goals: Get her first conference abstract accepted

personas.goals: Working sensors and a working airboat

beats.summary: How many are down; Wes undercounts, then the cost
The backlog and storage; Riya's storage number stands
Abstracts; Tomasz's travel budget figure is high and is corrected later
The April incident; first aid; airboat hours

turns.speaker: Adaeze
turns.text: Let's start with the sensors. Wes, how many are down?

turns.speaker: Wes
turns.text: Three, as of last week. The ones out by the channel.

turns.speaker: Tomasz
turns.text: The pipeline shows seven with no data since winter. Three are the ones you've visited.

turns.speaker: Wes
turns.text: Seven. I haven't been out to the far ones since the water came up.

turns.speaker: Adaeze
turns.text: Out of thirty-two, that's a lot.

turns.speaker: Riya
turns.text: How much is a replacement?

turns.speaker: Wes
turns.text: Four hundred and twenty each.

turns.speaker: Tomasz
turns.text: So almost three thousand to replace all seven.

turns.speaker: Adaeze
turns.text: Can any of them be repaired instead?

turns.speaker: Wes
turns.text: Maybe two. The others have water in the housing. That's the end of them.

turns.speaker: Adaeze
turns.text: Then we replace five and try to repair two.

turns.speaker: Wes
turns.text: I'll order the five sensors this week and take the two broken ones to the electronics shop.

turns.speaker: Tomasz
turns.text: We should really think about moving the sensors to higher ground at some point.

turns.speaker: Adaeze
turns.text: Data. Tomasz, where's the backlog?

turns.speaker: Tomasz
turns.text: Five months of sensor data is unprocessed. The pipeline broke when the university changed servers.

turns.speaker: Riya
turns.text: And we're at about ninety percent of our storage.

turns.speaker: Adaeze
turns.text: Ninety? Then we can't even store new data for long.

turns.speaker: Tomasz
turns.text: Fixing the pipeline is a week of work. Then the backlog runs by itself over a weekend.

turns.speaker: Adaeze
turns.text: Then the pipeline is your priority this week, ahead of the abstract.

turns.speaker: Tomasz
turns.text: Ahead of the abstract. Fine, but the deadline's tight.

turns.speaker: Riya
turns.text: Could the raw data go to the archive service, to free up space?

turns.speaker: Tomasz
turns.text: Yes, the older files can. I'll do that when the pipeline's back.

turns.speaker: Wes
turns.text: Did anyone see the cooking show where they made jambalaya with crawfish from a bayou? I swear it was our bayou.

turns.speaker: Riya
turns.text: My roommate watches it every night. The host keeps saying "y'all" wrong.

turns.speaker: Adaeze
turns.text: Okay. Conference. The abstract deadline is June sixth. We planned three.

turns.speaker: Tomasz
turns.text: Mine, Riya's, and the sensor network one with Wes.

turns.speaker: Riya
turns.text: Do I really have to submit one? I've never presented.

turns.speaker: Adaeze
turns.text: You do. You're ready, and a poster is a gentle start.

turns.speaker: Riya
turns.text: A poster. Okay. I can do a poster.

turns.speaker: Tomasz
turns.text: And the travel budget is ten thousand, so all three of us can go.

turns.speaker: Wes
turns.text: I'd rather not go. Somebody has to keep the sensors alive.

turns.speaker: Riya
turns.text: Maybe Wes could present remotely?

turns.speaker: Adaeze
turns.text: I checked the grant account this morning. Travel has sixty-five hundred left, not ten.

turns.speaker: Tomasz
turns.text: Sixty-five hundred. That's two people, not three.

turns.speaker: Adaeze
turns.text: Then Riya and Tomasz go, and the sensor abstract is presented by Tomasz.

turns.speaker: Tomasz
turns.text: Fair enough.

turns.speaker: Adaeze
turns.text: Safety. I want to talk about April twenty-second.

turns.speaker: Wes
turns.text: I slipped off the boardwalk into the channel. I'm fine. It was my fault.

turns.speaker: Adaeze
turns.text: It wasn't a fault. It was a wet boardwalk and no second person. That's on the process.

turns.speaker: Riya
turns.text: How many of us have first-aid certification?

turns.speaker: Wes
turns.text: Four. Me, Tomasz, and the two undergrads from last summer, who've left.

turns.speaker: Adaeze
turns.text: So really two, out of seven of us.

turns.speaker: Tomasz
turns.text: Could the department pay for a first-aid course for everyone?

turns.speaker: Adaeze
turns.text: They should. I'll ask the chair this week.

turns.speaker: Wes
turns.text: And nobody goes out alone. That should be a rule.

turns.speaker: Adaeze
turns.text: From today, nobody goes to the field alone, and the boardwalk sites need two people.

turns.speaker: Riya
turns.text: What about the airboat? We have forty hours left. Does that need two people too?

turns.speaker: Wes
turns.text: The airboat always has two. You can't drive and anchor at the same time.

turns.speaker: Tomasz
turns.text: Is the department going to fix the boardwalk itself?

turns.speaker: Adaeze
turns.text: Okay. Thank you, all. Wes, please be careful out there.

turns.speaker: Wes
turns.text: Always.
